subject: Biology
description: Liver functions, bile, hepatocytes, pancreas exocrine + endocrine roles, insulin/glucagon

questions.stem: The LARGEST internal organ of the human body, lying mostly under the right lower ribs, is the:

options.option_text: Stomach, the J-shaped digestive sac in the upper abdomen
Liver, weighing about 1.4 kg in a typical adult body
Right kidney, located at the back of the abdominal cavity
Pancreas, lying horizontally behind the lower stomach

questions.explanation: Liver — largest internal organ, ~1.4 kg in adult, lies in the right upper quadrant. (Skin is the largest organ overall, but is external.) Functions: bile production, detoxification, glycogen storage, plasma protein synthesis, drug metabolism. Hepatocytes are the main functional cells. Distractor 1 = stomach (smaller). Distractor 3 = kidney (much smaller, ~150 g). Distractor 4 = pancreas (~80 g).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: BILE produced by the liver is primarily stored and concentrated in the:

options.option_text: Spleen, an organ near the upper-left abdomen
Gallbladder, the small sac just under the liver
Pancreas, the long gland behind the stomach
Duodenum, the first short loop of small intestine

questions.explanation: Bile is made by liver cells continuously, stored + concentrated in the gallbladder, released into the duodenum after meals (especially fatty ones) via the common bile duct. Bile contains bile salts (emulsify fats, helping lipase enzymes break them down), bilirubin (waste from RBC breakdown), cholesterol. GALLSTONES — cholesterol or pigment stones in gallbladder; common surgical condition. Distractor 1 — spleen filters blood + recycles RBCs. Distractor 3 — pancreas makes pancreatic juice (different). Distractor 4 — bile is RELEASED into duodenum, not stored there.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The pancreas is unusual because it is BOTH an exocrine and an endocrine gland. Its endocrine portion is the:

options.option_text: Acinar cells, which secrete digestive enzymes
Islets of Langerhans, secreting insulin and glucagon
Bile-duct cells, which transport liver bile to gut
Goblet cells, which secrete mucus into intestinal lumen

questions.explanation: Pancreas — DUAL function. EXOCRINE (~95% of mass): acinar cells secrete pancreatic juice (containing trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, amylase, lipase) into ducts → duodenum. ENDOCRINE (~5%): Islets of Langerhans (~1 million scattered clusters), secrete hormones DIRECTLY into bloodstream — INSULIN (β-cells, lowers blood glucose), GLUCAGON (α-cells, raises blood glucose), SOMATOSTATIN (δ-cells), Pancreatic Polypeptide. Distractor 1 — exocrine. Distractor 3 — bile ducts are liver-related. Distractor 4 — goblet cells are intestinal.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: INSULIN, secreted by pancreatic β-cells, lowers blood glucose by:

options.option_text: Breaking down glucose immediately into water and CO₂
Helping body cells absorb glucose from the blood
Stopping the pancreas from secreting any more glucose
Converting fats into glucose for ready energy use

questions.explanation: Insulin binds receptors on muscle, fat, and liver cells → triggers GLUT4 glucose transporters to move to cell membrane → glucose enters cells. Excess glucose stored as glycogen (liver/muscle) or fat (adipose). Diabetes mellitus type 1 = autoimmune β-cell destruction → little/no insulin (insulin-dependent). Type 2 = insulin resistance + relative deficiency. Discovered by Banting + Best (Toronto, 1921, Nobel 1923). Distractor 1 — that's cellular respiration. Distractor 3 — pancreas doesn't 'secrete glucose'. Distractor 4 — gluconeogenesis is the OPPOSITE direction (fats/proteins → glucose), not insulin's role.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Liver detoxifies many toxins. Common alcohol (ethanol) is processed in the liver mainly by the enzyme:

options.option_text: Pepsin, the enzyme that digests proteins in the stomach
Alcohol dehydrogenase, the first enzyme of ethanol breakdown
Lipase, the enzyme that breaks down dietary fat in the gut
Salivary amylase, the enzyme that acts on starch in the mouth

questions.explanation: ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE (ADH) — converts ethanol to ACETALDEHYDE (toxic intermediate). Then ALDEHYDE DEHYDROGENASE (ALDH) → ACETATE → eventually CO₂ + water. Genetic variants of ALDH2 in East Asian populations cause acetaldehyde build-up after drinking → flushed face + nausea. Drug DISULFIRAM (Antabuse) blocks ALDH; combined with alcohol gives violent reaction → used in alcoholism treatment. Distractor 1 = stomach protein digestion. Distractor 3 = fat digestion. Distractor 4 = mouth carbohydrate digestion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: JAUNDICE, in which the skin and eyes turn yellowish, is most directly caused by elevated blood levels of:

options.option_text: Insulin from the pancreas, raising bilirubin levels
Bilirubin, a yellow pigment from RBC breakdown
Carotene from yellow and orange-coloured vegetables
Cholesterol from a diet rich in saturated animal fat

questions.explanation: Bilirubin — yellow pigment from haemoglobin breakdown (when old RBCs are destroyed in spleen + liver). Liver normally conjugates it and excretes it via bile. When liver is damaged (hepatitis), bile duct blocked (gallstones), or RBC destruction is high (haemolysis), bilirubin accumulates → yellow tinge in tissues with thin epidermis (sclera of eyes, then skin). Investigated by liver function tests (LFTs). Distractor 1 — insulin doesn't change skin colour. Distractor 3 — excess carotene CAN cause yellowing (carotenoderma) but that's harmless and rare. Distractor 4 — cholesterol-related skin signs (xanthelasma) are localised yellow spots, not generalised jaundice.

questions.stem: Hepatitis A and Hepatitis E are both viral infections of the liver that spread mostly via:

options.option_text: Sharing contaminated injection needles in clinics
Faecally-contaminated food and drinking water
Sexual contact between infected individuals
Pregnant mother passing the virus to her foetus

questions.explanation: Hepatitis A and E — FAECAL-ORAL transmission (contaminated food/water). Common in low-sanitation regions. Hep A — vaccine available; Hep E — particularly dangerous in pregnant women (high mortality). HEP B, C, D — blood-borne (needles, transfusion, sexual). Hep B has a widely used vaccine; Hep C had no vaccine but excellent direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) since 2014. Distractor 1 = Hep B/C/D. Distractor 3 = Hep B/C/D. Distractor 4 = vertical transmission (mainly Hep B).
